title: Terms Settled by Counsel for the Retirement of Equity Held Under Membership and Patronage Equity
content:
Equity held under Membership and Patronage Equity is retired ahead of the cycle in only the cases the class allows.

**On age.** A member who has reached the class's retirement age may apply, the age being taken from the year of birth on their own record and measured at the close of the current fiscal year, and the equity is paid over the class's number of annual instalments less the class's age retirement discount.

**On death.** The estate applies within the class's notice period counted in whole calendar days from the recorded date of death, and the estate's application is considered only once the class's required estate documentation is lodged and recorded. A relative telephoning to say the member has died is not that documentation, however well known the family is at the counter, and nothing is retired on it.

**On early retirement.** Where the class allows it at all, early retirement carries the class's early retirement discount and is at the board's discretion rather than the member's right.

**Board approval.** Every retirement is approved by the board before it is paid where the class requires board approval, and the desk records the application rather than promising an outcome.

**Where no route exists.** A member whose class allows no early retirement and who is under the retirement age has no route to their equity except the ordinary cycle, and a request to shorten it is one no policy settles.

**The class figures.** The retirement age, the age discount, the instalments, whether death retirement is open, the notice period, the early retirement permission and its discount are the figures the class carries.

## The authority for the estate condition

What is lodged and recorded is read from the cooperative's own register of equity applications before anything is retired: the application must stand as an estate retirement application, registered and signed by the member's estate, and the notice of death must stand recorded on the membership. The application is identified by its own reference so that what is read belongs to the retirement being considered.

## Boundary cases on hypothetical dates

Where the class allows 365 calendar days from the recorded date of death, an application registered on the 365th day is inside the period and one registered on the 366th is outside it; the period is counted in whole calendar days from the recorded date of death and from no other date. A member whose recorded year of birth puts them at 69 at the close of the current fiscal year has not reached a class age of 70; at 70 they have, the boundary itself satisfying the condition.
